# Tabs

Switches between views of the same thing on one page.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill">In Brand expressive</span></p>

## See it live

<div class="odv-live"><span class="odv-wait">Start Storybook to see it live: <code>npm run storybook</code></span><iframe src="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-tabs--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:brand-expressive;mode:light" title="Tabs examples in Storybook" loading="lazy"></iframe><div class="bar"><span>Live from Storybook</span><a href="http://localhost:6006/?path=/docs/components-tabs--docs">Open Tabs in Storybook</a><a href="http://localhost:6006/iframe.html?id=components-tabs--examples&viewMode=story&globals=scheme:brand-expressive;mode:dark">See it in dark</a></div></div>

## When to use it

**In Brand expressive:** A few related views of one drop, such as line-up and countdown. Not for links to other pages.

- **Use it when:** Related views of one object that people move between.
- **Not when:** Navigation to other pages (links), or steps of a task (progress).

Instead:

- [Accordion](./accordion.md): Stacked sections people can open together.
- [Navigation menu](./navigation-menu.md): Other pages.

## Words

- Headlines are short and bold. Three to six words.
- Verbs that move: Join, Try, Go.
- Playful in headlines, plain in errors.
- Use: Join, Drop, Go, Love. Avoid: Synergy, Leverage, Kindly.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Go
- `content.action.cancel`: Not now
- `content.action.destroy`: Remove
- `content.action.retry`: Try again
- `content.action.empty-action`: Explore the drop

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Arrow keys move between tabs; Tab moves into the panel. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It is a tablist; the selected tab owns its panel. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add tabs
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Tabs reads 14 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Tabs's tokens to change Tabs alone.
